item.title: FusionAdvisor: Decision guidance for efficient operator fusion in deep models
item.description:
Chang Jiang, Yanan Yang, Shen Gao, Jianjiang Li, Jie Wu
Big Data Mining and Analytics
DOI: 10.26599/bdma.2026.9020025
Abstract As deep learning models grow in size and complexity, optimizing the execution efficiency becomes critical. Operator fusion merges multiple operators to reduce memory overhead and enhance computational efficiency. However, the combinatorial explosion of possible fusion combinations in modern models creates a search space that challenges traditional manual and heuristic methods. We propose FusionAdvisor, a neural network based framework that predicts the speedups of candidate fusion strategies from computation graphs and recommends the top- candidates (recommended strategies). Trained on our constructed fusion strategy dataset, it abstracts fusion selection as a service, enabling developers to choose high-performance strategies and accelerate inference efficiently. Experimental results demonstrate that FusionAdvisor’s neural network predicts post-fusion speedups with low error, enabling promising strategy recommendations while maintaining search efficiency comparable to the existing methods. This work advances automated operator fusion selection, reduces optimization costs, and improves resource utilization in complex scenarios, including Large Language Models (LLMs) and other large-scale models.

item.title: Multi-view fusion and distillation for subgrade distresses detection based on 3D ground-penetrating radar
item.description:
Chunpeng Zhou, Kangjie Ning, Haishuai Wang, Zhi Yu, Sheng Zhou, Jiajun Bu
Big Data Mining and Analytics
DOI: 10.26599/bdma.2026.9020039
Abstract The Three-Dimensional Ground-Penetrating Radar (3D-GPR) has been widely used for subgrade distress detection. To enhance the efficiency and accuracy of detection, pioneering studies have attempted to adopt automatic detection techniques such as deep learning. However, existing works typically rely on traditional One-Dimensional (1D) A-scan, Two-Dimensional (2D)-B-scan or 3D C-scan GPR data, resulting in either insufficient spatial information or high computational complexity. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel methodology for subgrade distress detection by leveraging multi-view information from vanilla 3D-GPR data. First, we construct a real multi-view image dataset derived from the vanilla 3D-GPR data for the detection task, providing richer spatial information compared to A-scan and B-scan data, and reducing data computational complexity compared to C-scan data. Subsequently, we develop a novel Multi-View Fusion and Distillation Ground-Penetrating Radar framework, called GPR-MVFD, specifically designed to optimally utilize the multi-view GPR dataset. This framework ingeniously incorporates the attention-based fusion and multi-view distillation to facilitate significant feature extraction for subgrade distresses. In addition, a self-adaptive learning mechanism is adopted to stabilize the model training and prevent performance degeneration in each branch. Extensive experiments demonstrate the value of the newly constructed GPR dataset and showcase the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed GPR-MVFD. Notably, our framework outperforms not only the existing GPR baselines, but also the state-of-the-art methods in the fields of multi-view learning, multimodal learning, and Knowledge Distillation (KD). Our data and code have been made publicly available as open source at https://github.com/zhouchunpong/multi-view-3DGPR.
